title: Inverse identities and arbitrary pullback for line-quotient charts
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal E$ an arbitrary quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $p:P=\operatorname{Proj}_S A_S(\mathcal E)\to S$, where $A_S(\mathcal E)$ is the canonical symmetric graded algebra [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra] and relative Proj is [def-nagata-relative-proj]. No finite-type or local-freeness hypothesis is imposed on $\mathcal E$. Let $D=(Q,q_P)$ be any normalized tautological quotient datum on $P$ [def-per-projective-bundle-quotient-data]. For every scheme $T$, morphism $h:T\to S$, invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and surjection $q:h^*\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow L$, denote by $F_h(L,q)$ the morphism characterized by the homogeneous-fraction formulas of [lem-trf-line-quotient-homogeneous-fraction-map]. For any $S$-morphism $a:T\to P$, its pulled map $q_a:h^*\mathcal E\to a^*Q$, formed using $(p\circ a)^*\simeq a^*p^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], is surjective and $a^*Q$ is invertible. There is a quotient-compatible isomorphism
$$\theta_q:F_h(L,q)^*Q\xrightarrow{\sim}L,\qquad \theta_q\circ F_h(L,q)^*q_P=q.$$
Its chart normalization is as follows: for $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, $M=\mathcal E(U)$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset h^{-1}U$ with a frame $l$ of $L$, $q(v\otimes1)=b_v l$ for every $v\in M$, and $e=\iota(m)$ for $m\in M$, on $W_m=D(b_m)$ it sends the pulled frame $e$ to $b_m l$. It carries the pulled quotient of $v\in M$ to $(b_v/b_m)b_m l=b_vl$. These isomorphisms agree on every overlap, with $e/f$ pulling back to $b_m/b_n$ for $n\in M$, $f=\iota(n)$, and with changes of frame and base. Conversely,
$$F_h(a^*Q,q_a)=a.$$
On the inverse image of $D_+(e)$ the frame is $a^*e$, the coefficient of $e$ is $1$, and the recovered ring map sends every $c/e^d$ to $a^*(c/e^d)$ for $c\in\operatorname{Sym}^d_R M$. If $v:L\xrightarrow{\sim}L'$ satisfies $vq=q'$, then $F_h(L,q)=F_h(L',q')$; under frames $l,v(l)$ the coefficient maps coincide. For every scheme morphism $u:T'\to T$, put $q'=u^*q:(h\circ u)^*\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow u^*L$ using the canonical composite-pullback identification. Then
$$F_{h\circ u}(u^*L,q')=F_h(L,q)\circ u,\qquad \theta_{q'}=u^*\theta_q$$
under the canonical pullback identifications. For $z\in\operatorname{Sym}^d_R M$, let $b(z)$ be its coefficient in the induced graded map into $L^{\otimes d}$ in the frame $l^{\otimes d}$. On the pulled-back charts the coefficient map sends $b(z)/b_m^d$ to $u^*b(z)/(u^*b_m)^d$ and the frame isomorphism sends $e$ to $u^*q(m)$. No flatness of $u$ or finite generation of $\mathcal E$ is required.

proof.text: Use the invertibility clause of the existing public theorem invertible_pullback_tensor [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] directly, without restating preservation of invertibility and left adjointness preserves epimorphisms as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-epi-direct-sum]. The composite comparison is [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition]. Its normalized unit equation computes the pulled quotient on every original section. The inverse scalar function of a frame then gives coefficient one for its own pulled tautological generator.

Apply [lem-trf-line-quotient-recovered-charts] to the quotient pulled along a. It supplies the fraction charts at a and every recovered coefficient. Uniqueness of the chart morphism in [lem-trf-line-quotient-homogeneous-fraction-map] identifies any supplied F with a.

By [lem-trf-line-quotient-fraction-kernel], the pulled quotient and q annihilate exactly the same morphisms. Each epimorphism in the abelian category of module sheaves is a normal epimorphism, hence a cokernel of some map. That defining map is killed by the first quotient and therefore by the second. The cokernel universal property factors each quotient through the other. Cancellation of each epimorphism proves that the two factorizations are inverse. Package this construction as an existence theorem over an arbitrary category with zero morphisms in which all epimorphisms are normal and eliminate that theorem in the scheme-module application; thus downstream normalization uses an abstract compatible isomorphism. Evaluating their quotient equality on sections proves theta(e_m)=b_m l. When b_m is a unit, transport the unit multiple of the frame through theta inverse; scalar associativity gives both ratio equations.

Apply [lem-trf-line-quotient-iso-charts] for coefficient equality and fraction charts at the same F in the new quotient line. Use chart-morphism uniqueness from [lem-trf-line-quotient-homogeneous-fraction-map] to identify F prime with F.

Apply [lem-trf-line-quotient-pullback-charts] to obtain fraction charts at u;F and all homogeneous and generator coefficient equations. Construct Localization.awayMap of u.appLE; its scalar equation and value on each homogeneous fraction follow from the localization map equations. Uniqueness from [lem-trf-line-quotient-homogeneous-fraction-map] gives F prime=u;F. The normalized adjunction unit and naturality compute the composite pulled quotient followed by the pulled theta as exactly the pulled q. Transport along the morphism equality and cancel the epimorphic pulled tautological quotient. This identifies every compatible theta prime with the prescribed comparison followed by u^*theta. Its normalization follows again from its quotient equality.
